checks.detail: 1 phase had the tools designed for them

breakdown.label: States that both async and defer let a classic script be fetched in parallel with HTML parsing, so the fetch does not block the parser, unlike a classic script with src and neither attribute.
breakdown.detail: met, backed by verified evidence E1, E11. “Both `async` and `defer` eliminate this parser-blocking behavior for the download phase.”

breakdown.label: States that a defer script executes only after the document has finished parsing, and before DOMContentLoaded fires.
breakdown.detail: met, backed by verified evidence E3, E7. “Deferred scripts execute just before the DOMContentLoaded event fires”

breakdown.label: States that an async script executes as soon as it is available, interrupting parsing if parsing is still in progress, so it may run before or after DOMContentLoaded.
breakdown.detail: met, backed by verified evidence E1, E5, E7. “async scripts can interrupt DOM building if they finish downloading while the parser is still processing HTML”

breakdown.label: States that multiple defer scripts execute in document order, while async scripts execute in the order their downloads complete, which is not predictable.
breakdown.detail: met, backed by verified evidence E4, E6. “Deferred scripts maintain execution order: if you have three deferred scripts in sequence in the HTML, they will execute in that same sequence. Async scripts offer no such guarantee”

breakdown.label: States that async and defer have no effect on a classic inline script (a script element without a src attribute).
breakdown.detail: met, backed by verified evidence E2. “Inline scripts (scripts without a `src` attribute) do not support the `async` or `defer` attributes; these attributes are ignored for inline classic scripts.”

breakdown.label: States that module scripts are deferred by default, so the defer attribute has no effect on them, while the async attribute does apply to module scripts.
breakdown.detail: met, backed by verified evidence E8, E9, E10. “The `defer` attribute has no effect on module scripts since they already defer by default. If you add the `async` attribute to an external module script”

evidence.claim: The async attribute causes external classic scripts to be fetched in parallel to parsing and evaluated as soon as they are available, potentially before parsing completes
evidence.quote: For external classic scripts, if the async attribute is present, then the classic script will be fetched in parallel to parsing and evaluated as soon as it is available (potentially before parsing completes).

evidence.claim: The async attribute must not be used on inline scripts as it would have no effect
evidence.quote: Warning: This attribute must not be used if the src attribute is absent (i.e., for inline scripts) for classic scripts, in this case it would have no effect.

evidence.claim: The defer attribute causes scripts to execute after the document has been parsed but before the DOMContentLoaded event
evidence.quote: This Boolean attribute is set to indicate to a browser that the script is meant to be executed after the document has been parsed, but before firing DOMContentLoaded event.

evidence.claim: Deferred scripts execute in the order they appear in the document
evidence.quote: Scripts with the defer attribute will execute in the order in which they appear in the document.

evidence.claim: Async scripts can interrupt DOM building if they finish downloading while the parser is still at work
evidence.quote: It also means they can interrupt DOM building if they finish downloading while the parser is still at work.

evidence.claim: Async scripts do not execute in a guaranteed order when there are multiple scripts
evidence.quote: Scripts with the async attribute execute at the first opportunity after they finish downloading and before the window's load event. This means it's possible (and likely) that async scripts won't run in the order in which they appear in the HTML.

evidence.claim: DOMContentLoaded fires after deferred scripts execute but before async scripts execute
evidence.quote: DOMContentLoaded is fired after the execution of these scripts, but before the execution of scripts with async.

evidence.claim: Module scripts are deferred by default and the defer attribute has no effect on them
evidence.quote: The defer attribute has no effect on module scripts — they defer by default.

evidence.claim: Module scripts with async attribute fetch and execute like async classic scripts
evidence.quote: For module scripts, if the async attribute is present, then the module script and all its dependencies will be fetched in parallel to parsing, and the module script will be evaluated as soon as it is available (potentially before parsing completes).

evidence.claim: Module scripts without async execute in order after HTML parsing completes
evidence.quote: Otherwise, the module script and its dependencies will be fetched in parallel to parsing and evaluated when the page has finished parsing.

evidence.claim: Module scripts are deferred automatically and scripts without async or defer are parser-blocking
evidence.quote: async and defer allow external scripts to load without blocking the HTML parser while scripts (including inline scripts) with type="module" are deferred automatically.

evidence.claim: Inline scripts without type="module" block the parser until parsed and executed
evidence.quote: When using inline JavaScript, the parser is similarly blocked until the inline script is parsed and executed.

evidence.claim: When both async and defer are specified, the element acts as if only async is specified
evidence.quote: If the attribute is specified with the defer attribute, the element will act as if only the async attribute is specified.
